text:
Noah Ostlund's season split into two halves. He opened with a much bigger job than last year, 18 minutes a night and a regular spot on Buffalo's power play, and then his ice time slid to about 14 minutes over the last four games.

He's been cold: no goals in his last ten, three assists, on 5.3 expected points. The underlying reason looks like luck more than play. The Sabres have scored 8.5 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and his own shooting is at 8.9% against a typical 13.5%.

He's still at 12 points in 23 games, above the 0.31 median for forwards picked around him in their first full season. Evolving-Hockey had his value last season coming from defense, which isn't what you'd expect from a 22-year-old Swedish playmaker. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds the fun part: 20% of his setups crossed the royal road, against 7% for a typical forward, the pass that moves a goalie side to side.

What to watch: whether the minutes come back. The process says they should.
